title: Thessaloniki courthouse protest against the campus-security law
location: Outside a courthouse in Thessaloniki, Greece; exact courthouse and route are not stated.
scope: One local Thessaloniki courthouse gathering on February 23. Keep separate from the February 22 education-law demonstration and university occupation mentioned as background.
participants_original: More than 5,000 university students and other protesters
threshold_50_evidence: The contemporary report explicitly says more than 5,000 students and other protesters gathered outside a courthouse in Thessaloniki, exceeding the 50-person threshold. This is a published lower-bound statement, not an exact total.

start_date.summary: The article is published on February 23 and identifies the described Thessaloniki courthouse protest as Tuesday's protest.

location.summary: The article places the gathering outside a courthouse in Thessaloniki, Greece's second-largest city; it does not identify the exact courthouse.

scope.summary: This is the February 23 courthouse gathering; the article separately refers to a demonstration on Monday, February 22.

demands.summary: The article says participants rallied against the new campus-security law.

participants_original.summary: The article reports more than 5,000 university students and other protesters.

participants_min.summary: The published lower-bound claim is over 5,000; stored as at least 5,001 persons, with no upper bound or exact total.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The reported lower bound is far above the inclusion threshold of 50.

organizer.summary: No organizer is identified in the article; leave unknown.

end_date.summary: The story does not state when participants left or when the physical gathering ended.

protester_violence.summary: The article says the separate February 22 demonstration turned violent but does not identify who used violence; it makes no event-specific violence claim about the February 23 gathering.

state_response.summary: The article says the Feb23 gathering was banned under pandemic restrictions, but gives no event-specific account of enforcement, accommodation, arrests on Feb23, dispersal, ignore, beatings, killings or shootings. It attributes 31 arrests to the prior day's separate demonstration.

notes: Euronews credits AP; treat this as AP-origin reporting, not independent corroboration. The reported 31 arrests and the unspecified violence belong to the prior-day February 22 demonstration, not this February 23 courthouse event. Although the article says the gathering was banned under pandemic restrictions, it does not describe the police response to the February 23 assembly.
open_questions: Can a distinct contemporary source confirm the Feb23 attendance and exact courthouse location?
Was there any actual state response to this gathering beyond the stated pandemic ban?
What were the physical beginning and end times, and who organized it?
